candidateDecisions.label: Digital society, artificial intelligence and culture

analysis: Media, Culture and Society connects introductory film language and media archaeology with representation, documentary, rhetorical communication and audience or consumer inquiry. It draws on sociology, politics, psychology and both qualitative and quantitative methods. Adding Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations supplies the Market Research prerequisite and media industry context. The sustainability option combines climate, Earth systems, mapping, chemical and resource analysis with energy, adaptation, law, public economics and environmental justice. Energy & Sustainability replaces the advanced project with an applied account of renewable supply, storage and constraints, after the sustainability foundation. The digital option connects programming, algorithms, machine learning, vision and AI ethics with documentary, online representation and digital public spheres. Introduction to Data Science adds hands-on work with data before specialised machine learning. This replaces a general stylistics course while retaining media and social breadth. The respective pairwise differences are 19, 13 and 22 courses. The culture and society direction has substantive themes but overlaps the first option and falls beyond the three-option cap. Alignments distinguish media studies, documentary history and material media from curating and archiving practice. Utrecht requires a paper in each of the interdisciplinary and media components. UCR independent research is optional and outside the schedule.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce film analysis. UCR also covers television and digital media.
Both examine audiovisual media through their material and technological history.
Both study documentary film. Utrecht focuses on curating it, while UCR studies documentary forms, history and ethics.
Utrecht develops interdisciplinary approaches to research. UCR develops related skills across philosophy and methods courses.
Utrecht studies how media represent the past.
Utrecht studies how performance is archived.
Utrecht students choose an approved course within their main direction.
Utrecht requires 15 EC outside the humanities main direction in social science. UCR illustrates social science through its selected courses.
Both develop research skills. UCR covers qualitative social inquiry, while Utrecht introduces media research.
Utrecht applies multiple disciplinary perspectives in a required project. UCR offers related problem-based inquiry across courses.
Utrecht requires 15 EC in science outside the humanities main direction. UCR illustrates science and quantitative inquiry through different courses.
Both develop academic writing and communication. Utrecht uses a dedicated writing academy.
Utrecht requires an interdisciplinary paper after De denkacademie and at least 120 EC. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled plan.
Utrecht leaves this space open for choices such as electives, a minor or an internship within programme rules.
Utrecht develops a media research proposal after the core package.
Utrecht requires a separate media final paper after the research seminar.
